chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Ibn Abi Najran and Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

Regarding a man who had a slave girl under his ownership, so he divorced her according to the Sunnah, then she became irrevocably divorced from him, then he bought her after that before she married another husband. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) has judged regarding this: a Verse permits her and another Verse prohibits her, and I myself and my sons would prohibit from her.'

key_terms.بَانَتْ مِنْهُ: She became irrevocably divorced from him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a master divorcing and then buying back his slave girl?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the juristic nuance of *iddah* (waiting period) for a slave girl divorced by her master, where repurchasing her before she marries another creates a legal ambiguity. It cites Imam Ali’s ruling that while two Quranic verses appear to permit and prohibit the union respectively, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) explicitly forbade it for himself and his progeny, establishing a specific precedent in Shia fiqh. This reflects the principle of *naskh* (abrogation) or contextual application where prophetic practice overrides apparent textual contradictions.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Ibn Abu Najran, and Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Sinan,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said regarding a man under who used to be a slave girl. So he divorced her upon the Sunnah, then she was irrevocably divorced from him. They he bought her after that before she married another husband. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> had judged regarding this (as there is) A Verse Permits her and another Verse Prohibits her, and I<sup>asws</sup> would prohibit from her myself<sup>asws</sup> and my<sup>asws</sup> sons<sup>asws</sup>’.
